$i -lt $idx.LineCount; $i++) { $idx.Offsets[$i] = $br.ReadInt64() }\r\n   73:         } finally { $br.Dispose(); $fs.Dispose() }\r\n   74:         return $idx\r\n   75:     }\r\n   76: \r\n   77:     [long] Offset([int]$Line) {\r\n   78:         if ($Line -lt 0 -or $Line -ge $this.LineCount) {\r\n   79:             throw \"Line $Line out of range [0, $($this.LineCount - 1)]\"\r\n   80:         }\r\n   81:         return $this.Offsets[$Line]\r\n   82:     }\r\n   83: }\r\n   84: \r\n   85: $script:NsjSettings = $null\r\n   86: $script:NsjFallbacks = 0      # records that dropped from the Newtonsoft fast path to the cmdlet\r\n   87: $script:NsjLastError = $null  # last fast-path failure message (diagnostic)\r\n   88: \r\n   89: function Write-JsonlStage {\r\n   90:     <#\r\n   91:     .SYNOPSIS  Emit a stage's records as JSONL plus coordinated .jidx and .sig sidecars.\r\n   92:     .OUTPUTS   [pscustomobject] @{ Jsonl; Jidx; Sig; Records }\r\n   93:     #>\r\n   94:     [CmdletBinding()]\r\n   95:     param(\r\n   96:         [Parameter(Mandatory)] [AllowEmptyCollection()] [object[]] $Records,\r\n   97:         [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]   $OutputPath,\r\n   98:         [string] $SourcePath,\r\n   99:         [string] $Stage,\r\n  100:         [int]    $Depth = 12\r\n  101:     )\r\n  102:     $dir = [System.IO.Path]::GetDirectoryName($OutputPath)\r\n  103:     if ($dir -and -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $dir)) {\r\n  104:         New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $dir | Out-Null\r\n  105:     }\r\n  106: \r\n  107:     # Newtonsoft direct for dictionary records — byte-identical to ConvertTo-Json (PS7's cmdlet is\r\n  108:     # Newtonsoft-backed with StringEscapeHandling.Default: control chars escaped, <>&' LITERAL —\r\n  109:     # EscapeHtml was tried first and diverged on math glyphs; full-lane byte parity verified on the\r\n  110:     # 84p bench) minus ~160k cmdlet invocations per document. PSCustomObject records keep the\r\n  111:     # cmdlet path: Newtonsoft would serialize the PSObject wrapper, not the properties.\r\n  112:     if ($null -eq $script:NsjSettings -and ('Newtonsoft.Json.JsonConvert' -as [type])) {\r\n  113:         $script:NsjSettings = [Newtonsoft.Json.JsonSerializerSettings]::new()\r\n  114:         $script:NsjSettings.StringEscapeHandling = [Newtonsoft.Json.StringEscapeHandling]::Default\r\n  115:         $script:NsjSettings.Formatting = [Newtonsoft.Json.Formatting]::None\r\n  116:     }\r\n  117: \r\n  118:     # line-start offsets accumulate DURING the write (GetByteCount per line) — the writer knows\r\n  119:     # every length; re-scanning the finished file per-byte cost 17.5s on a 33MB lane\r\n  120:     $offsets = [System.Collections.Generic.List[long]]::new()\r\n  121:     $utf8 = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)\r\n  122:     $fbBefore = $script:NsjFallbacks\r\n  123:     $sw = [System.IO.StreamWriter]::new($OutputPath, $false, $utf8)\r\n  124:     try {\r\n  125:         $nlBytes = [long]$utf8.GetByteCount($sw.NewLine)\r\n  126:         $pos = 0L\r\n  127:         foreach ($r in $Records) {\r\n  128:             $json = $null\r\n  129:             if ($null -ne $script:NsjSettings -and $r -is [System.Collections.IDictionary]) {\r\n  130:                 # per-record fallback: a PSObject-wrapped value hiding in a dictionary makes\r\n  131:                 # Newtonsoft reflect the wrapper (self-referencing loop) — that record drops to\r\n  132:                 # the cmdlet path instead of failing the stage\r\n  133:                 try { $json = [Newtonsoft.Json.JsonConvert]::SerializeObject($r, $script:NsjSettings) }\r\n  134:                 catch { $json = $null; $script:NsjFallbacks++; $script:NsjLastError = $_.Exception.Message }\r\n  135:             }\r\n  136:             if ($null -eq $json) { $json = $r | ConvertTo-Json -Compress -Depth $Depth }\r\n  137:             $offsets.Add($pos)\r\n  138:             $pos += [long]$utf8.GetByteCount($json) + $nlBytes\r\n  139:             $sw.WriteLine($json)\r\n  140:         }\r\n  141:     } finally { $sw.Dispose() }\r\n  142: \r\n  143:     # loud, attributed telemetry: a fallback means some record carried a PSObject-wrapped value\r\n  144:     # (classic source: `$hash.Keys | Sort-Object` — pipeline output is wrapped). The output is\r\n  145:     # still correct, but the emitting stage should unwrap at the source. Tested by\r\n  146:     # tests/shared/encoding-invariants.Tests.ps1.\r\n  147:     $fbDelta = $script:NsjFallbacks - $fbBefore\r\n  148:     if ($fbDelta -gt 0) {\r\n  149:         Write-Warning \"Write-JsonlStage[$Stage -> $(Split-Path -Leaf $OutputPath)]: $fbDelta record(s) fell back from the Newtonsoft fast path (PSObject-wrapped value in a dictionary record; last error: $script:NsjLastError)\"\r\n  150:     }\r\n  151: \r\n  152:     $jidxPath = \"$OutputPath.jidx\"\r\n  153:     [JsonlIndex]::WriteIndex($jidxPath, $offsets)\r\n  154: \r\n  155:     $sig = [ordered]@{\r\n  156:         stage   = $Stage\r\n  157:         records = $Records.Count\r\n  158:         output  = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileName($OutputPath)\r\n  159:     }\r\n  160:     if ($SourcePath -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $SourcePath)) {\r\n  161:         $sig['source'] = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileName($SourcePath)\r\n  162:         $sig['source_sha256'] = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $SourcePath -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()\r\n  163:     }\r\n  164:     $sigPath = \"$OutputPath.sig\"\r\n  165:     [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($sigPath, ($sig | ConvertTo-Json), [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))\r\n  166: \r\n  167:     # inventory: every durable artifact self-registers here — the cross-cutting \"decorator\"\r\n  168:     # realised via the single write-chokepoint. Best-effort: the artifact is ground truth, the\r\n  169:     # inventory a convenience window onto the in-play objects (one per scratch dir).\r\n  170:     try {\r\n  171:         $invPath = Join-Path ([System.IO.Path]::GetDirectoryName($OutputPath)) 'inventory.json'\r\n  172:         $inv = if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $invPath) { [System.IO.File]::ReadAllText($invPath, [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)) | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable } else { @{} }\r\n  173:         $inv[[System.IO.Path]::GetFileName($OutputPath)] = @{\r\n  174:             stage   = $Stage\r\n  175:             records = $Records.Count\r\n  176:             bytes   = (Get-Item -LiteralPath $OutputPath).Length\r\n  177:             source  = if ($SourcePath) { [System.IO.Path]::GetFileName($SourcePath) } else { $null }\r\n  178:         }\r\n  179:         [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($invPath, ($inv | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6), [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))\r\n  180:     } catch { }\r\n  181: \r\n  182:     return [pscustomobject]@{ Jsonl = $OutputPath; Jidx = $jidxPath; Sig = $sigPath; Records = $Records.Count }\r\n  183: }\r\n  184: \r\n  185: function Read-JsonlRecord {\r\n  186:     <# Seek to record $At via the .jidx and return it parsed — O(1) random access. #>\r\n  187:     [CmdletBinding()]\r\n  188:     param(\r\n  189:         [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Path,\r\n  190:         [Parameter(Mandatory)] [int]    $At,\r\n  191:         [string] $IndexPath = \"$Path.jidx\"\r\n  192:     )\r\n  193:     $idx = [JsonlIndex]::Load($IndexPath)\r\n  194:     $fs = [System.IO.File]::OpenRead($Path)\r\n  195:     $sr = [System.IO.StreamReader]::new($fs, [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))\r\n  196:     try {\r\n  197:         [void]$fs.Seek($idx.Offset($At), [System.IO.SeekOrigin]::Begin)\r\n  198:         $sr.DiscardBufferedData()\r\n  199:         $line = $sr.ReadLine()\r\n  200:     } finally { $sr.Dispose() }\r\n  201:     return ($line | ConvertFrom-Json)\r\n  202: }\r\n  203: \r\n  204: function Get-JsonlSchema {\r\n  205:     <#\r\n  206:     .SYNOPSIS  Single-pass schema probe: per top-level key, the types seen and the\r\n  207:                share of records carrying it. Discovers the keys to walk without\r\n  208:                assuming them — a missing expected key shows as a coverage gap.\r\n  209:     #>\r\n  210:     [CmdletBinding()]\r\n  211:     param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Path)\r\n  212: \r\n  213:     $total = 0\r\n  214:     $count = @{}\r\n  215:     $types = @{}\r\n  216:     foreach ($line in [System.IO.File]::ReadLines($Path)) {\r\n  217:         if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($line)) { continue }\r\n  218:         $total++\r\n  219:         $obj = $line | ConvertFrom-Json\r\n  220:         foreach ($p in $obj.PSObject.Properties) {\r\n  221:             $k = $p.Name\r\n  222:             if (-not $count.ContainsKey($k)) { $count[$k] = 0 }\r\n  223:             $count[$k]++\r\n  224:             $tn = if ($null -eq $p.Value) { 'null' } else { $p.Value.GetType().Name }\r\n  225:             if (-not $types.ContainsKey($k)) { $types[$k] = @{} }\r\n  226:             if (-not $types[$k].ContainsKey($tn)) { $types[$k][$tn] = 0 }\r\n  227:             $types[$k][$tn]++\r\n  228:         }\r\n  229:     }\r\n  230:     foreach ($k in ($count.Keys | Sort-Object)) {\r\n  231:         [pscustomobject]@{\r\n  232:             Key      = $k\r\n  233:             Coverage = if ($total) { [math]::Round(100.0 * $count[$k] / $total, 1) } else { 0.0 }\r\n  234:             Types    = (($types[$k].Keys | Sort-Object) -join ',')\r\n  235:         }\r\n  236:     }\r\n  237: }\r\n  238: \r\n  239: # --- ledger: per-document milestone record (process position, written by the stages) ---\r\n  240: # A terse anti-amnesic ledger — not a verbose log. The process logs its own milestones as it\r\n  241: # passes them; the last line is \"where we are\", the whole file is \"how we got here\". One file\r\n  242: # per document, so fan-out never contends. Chunks stay ground truth; the ledger is the cheap\r\n  243: # process-position projection.\r\n  244: \r\n  245: function Add-LedgerEntry([string]$ChunksPath, [string]$Stage, [hashtable]$Extra = @{}) {\r\n  246:     $rec = [ordered]@{ stage = $Stage }\r\n  247:     foreach ($k in $Extra.Keys) { $rec[$k] = $Extra[$k] }\r\n  248:     $ledger = ($ChunksPath -replace '\\.chunks\\.jsonl$', '') + '.ledger.jsonl'\r\n  249:     [System.IO.File]::AppendAllText($ledger, (($rec | ConvertTo-Json -Compress -Depth 6) + \"`n\"), [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))\r\n  250: }\r\n  251: \r\n  252: function Get-LedgerStage([string]$ChunksPath) {\r\n  253:     $ledger = ($ChunksPath -replace '\\.chunks\\.jsonl$', '') + '.ledger.jsonl'\r\n  254:     if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $ledger)) { return $null }\r\n  255:     $last = [System.IO.File]::ReadLines($ledger) | Where-Object { $_ } | Select-Object -Last 1\r\n  256:     if ($last) { return ($last | ConvertFrom-Json) }\r\n  257:     return $null\r\n  258: }\r\n  259: \r\n  260: # the in-play artifacts registered alongside this document (the other window onto progress)\r\n  261: function Get-Inventory([string]$ChunksPath) {\r\n  262:     $invPath = Join-Path ([System.IO.Path]::GetDirectoryName($ChunksPath)) 'inventory.json'\r\n  263:     if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $invPath) { return [System.IO.File]::ReadAllText($invPath, [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)) | ConvertFrom-Json }\r\n  264:     return $null\r\n  265: }\r\n===== src/shared/runs.ps1 =====\r\n    1: #requires -Version 7.0\r\n    2: <#\r\n    3:   src/runs.ps1 — the run layout + paper addressing, as a standalone layer.\r\n    4: \r\n    5:   Every workflow pass lands its intermediate artifacts in a runstamped dir —\r\n    6:   {paper}/.runs/{yyyyMMdd_HHmmss}/ — beside the source it derives from. Non-destructive iteration\r\n    7:   by construction: a new run never touches a prior one; resolution is newest-run-wins unless the\r\n    8:   address pins a run ({paper}@{run}).\r\n    9: \r\n   10:   Split out of serving.ps1 so non-membrane lanes (the LaTeX converter's tarball unpacking) share\r\n   11:   the same layout without dragging the serving stack. Sources only the crawler.\r\n   12: #>\r\n   13: \r\n   14: . \"$PSScriptRoot/crawl.ps1\"\r\n   15: \r\n   16: # newest-first chunk paths for one paper, across .runs/* (stamp-descending)\r\n   17: function Get-RunChunks([string]$PaperDir, [string]$Slug) {\r\n   18:     $out = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()\r\n   19:     $runsRoot = Join-Path $PaperDir '.runs'\r\n   20:     if ([System.IO.Directory]::Exists($runsRoot)) {\r\n   21:         foreach ($d in ([System.IO.Directory]::EnumerateDirectories($runsRoot) | Sort-Object -Descending)) {\r\n   22:             $c = Join-Path $d \"$Slug.chunks.jsonl\"\r\n   23:             if ([System.IO.File]::Exists($c)) { $out.Add($c) }\r\n   24:         }\r\n   25:     }\r\n   26:     return $out\r\n   27: }\r\n   28: \r\n   29: function Get-LatestChunks([string]$PaperDir, [string]$Slug) {\r\n   30:     return @(Get-RunChunks $PaperDir $Slug) | Select-Object -First 1\r\n   31: }\r\n   32: \r\n   33: # --- module run layout: artifacts/{module}/runs/{stamp}/{slug}/ -------------------------------------\r\n   34: # The NEWER convention, and deliberately not the {paper}/.runs/{stamp} one below. Two reasons:\r\n   35: #\r\n   36: #   HYGIENE — regenerable working output does not belong interleaved with source. Under the old layout a\r\n   37: #   paper dir accumulated .runs/ alongside the tarball it was derived from; here everything regenerable\r\n   38: #   lands under artifacts/ (gitignored wholesale) and the source dir stays source.\r\n   39: #\r\n   40: #   DETERMINISM — the unpacked tarball is NOT a per-run artifact. Only genuinely per-run output (oracle counts, render logs) gets a runstamp.\r\n   43: #\r\n   44: # This breaks symmetry with the pig/gauntlet lanes, which still use {paper}/.runs. That is intentional\r\n   45: # while pdf conversion is shelved; it gets rebuilt onto this layout when that work resumes.\r\n   46: # The artifacts TIER itself — the directory runs live under, never its parent. Callers name this\r\n   47: # directly rather than naming a root that gets 'artifacts' appended: a parameter called \"repo root\"\r\n   48: # reads like \"write at the repo root\", which is the opposite of the hygiene this layout exists for.\r\n   49: function Get-ArtifactsRoot([string]$ArtifactsRoot = '') {\r\n   50:     if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($ArtifactsRoot)) { return [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath($ArtifactsRoot) }\r\n   51:     return (Join-Path ([System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath((Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '../..'))) 'artifacts')\r\n   52: }\r\n   53: \r\n   54: # {artifacts}/{module}/runs/{stamp}/{slug}/ — created fresh; a same-second collision bumps a suffix.\r\n   55: function New-ModuleRunDir([string]$Module, [string]$Slug, [string]$ArtifactsRoot = '') {\r\n   56:     if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($Module)) { throw 'module is required for a run dir' }\r\n   57:     $runsRoot = Join-Path (Get-ArtifactsRoot $ArtifactsRoot) $Module 'runs'\r\n   58:     $stamp = Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd_HHmmss'\r\n   59:     $leaf = if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($Slug)) { '' } else { $Slug }\r\n   60:     $dir = if ($leaf) { Join-Path $runsRoot $stamp $leaf } else { Join-Path $runsRoot $stamp }\r\n   61:     $n = 1\r\n   62:     while (Test-Path -LiteralPath $dir) {\r\n   63:         $n++\r\n   64:         $dir = if ($leaf) { Join-Path $runsRoot \"$stamp-$n\" $leaf } else { Join-Path $runsRoot \"$stamp-$n\" }\r\n   65:     }\r\n   66:     New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $dir | Out-Null\r\n   67:     return $dir\r\n   68: }\r\n   69: \r\n   70: # newest-first run dirs for one slug under a module, stamp-descending. Harnesses read newest-run-wins.\r\n   71: function Get-ModuleRunDirs([string]$Module, [string]$Slug, [string]$ArtifactsRoot = '') {\r\n   72:     $out = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()\r\n   73:     $runsRoot = Join-Path (Get-ArtifactsRoot $ArtifactsRoot) $Module 'runs'\r\n   74:     if ([System.IO.Directory]::Exists($runsRoot)) {\r\n   75:         foreach ($d in ([System.IO.Directory]::EnumerateDirectories($runsRoot) | Sort-Object -Descending)) {\r\n   76:             $slugDir = if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($Slug)) { $d } else { …1239 tokens truncated… }\r\n  166:     $p = $Paper -replace '\\\\', '/'\r\n  167:     if ($p -match '/') {\r\n  168:         $rootFull = [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath($Root)\r\n  169:         if ((Split-Path -Leaf $rootFull) -eq 'ingestion' -and $p -match '^ingestion/') { $p = $p.Substring(10) }\r\n  170:         $full = [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath((Join-Path $rootFull $p))\r\n  171:         $sep  = [System.IO.Path]::DirectorySeparatorChar\r\n  172:         if (-not (\"$full$sep\").StartsWith(($rootFull.TrimEnd($sep) + $sep), [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) {\r\n  173:             throw \"paper path escapes the ingestion root: '$Paper'\"\r\n  174:         }\r\n  175:         if (-not [System.IO.Directory]::Exists($full)) { throw \"paper dir not found: '$Paper'\" }\r\n  176:         return $full\r\n  177:     }\r\n  178:     if ($p -notmatch '^[\\w.\\-]+$') { throw \"invalid paper name: '$Paper'\" }\r\n  179:     # a paper dir is recognized by EITHER IR lane's raw — {slug}.json (opendataloader) beside the\r\n  180:     # source, or the pdfdig envelope {slug}.pdfdig.json (now under {slug}/.runs/*/pig/, git-ignored;\r\n  181:     # a retired beside-source copy still matches the second glob). Batch on-ramps should preprocess only docs the\r\n  15:   scan shows unprepped.\r\n  16: \r\n  17:     . ./preprocess.ps1\r\n  18:     Invoke-Preprocess -JsonPath <…/{slug}/{slug}.json>\r\n  19: #>\r\n  20: \r\n  21: . \"$PSScriptRoot/project-ir.ps1\"\r\n  22: . \"$PSScriptRoot/../pdfdig-adapter.ps1\"\r\n  23: . \"$PSScriptRoot/headings.ps1\"\r\n  24: . \"$PSScriptRoot/collapse.ps1\"\r\n  25: . \"$PSScriptRoot/zones.ps1\"\r\n  26: . \"$PSScriptRoot/sections.ps1\"\r\n  27: . \"$PSScriptRoot/normalize.ps1\"\r\n  28: . \"$PSScriptRoot/fidelity.ps1\"\r\n  29: . \"$PSScriptRoot/repair.ps1\"\r\n  30: . \"$PSScriptRoot/serving.ps1\"\r\n  31: \r\n  32: function Invoke-Preprocess {\r\n  33:     [CmdletBinding()] param(\r\n  34:         [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$JsonPath\r\n  35:     )\r\n  36:     if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $JsonPath)) { return [pscustomobject]@{ ok = $false; reason = \"source not found: $JsonPath\" } }\r\n  37:     $slug     = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($JsonPath)\r\n  38:     $srcDir   = Split-Path -Parent $JsonPath          # where the IR lanes sit: the paper dir (docling)\r\n  39:     $paperDir = Get-PaperDirFromIr $JsonPath          # or {paper}/.runs/{stamp}/pig (pig) — climbed out here\r\n  40: \r\n  41:     # IR lane by positional contract: {slug}.pdfdig.json = the pdfdig converter's envelope (its\r\n  42:     # classified run-nodes sit beside it, in the pig run dir); {slug}.json = the opendataloader raw\r\n  43:     # (beside the source). The membrane's OWN run layout keys off $paperDir, not the pig run dir.\r\n  44:     $lane = 'opendataloader'\r\n  45:     if ($slug.EndsWith('.pdfdig')) {\r\n  46:         $lane = 'pdfdig'\r\n  47:         $slug = $slug.Substring(0, $slug.Length - 7)\r\n  48:         $pigNodes = Join-Path $srcDir \"$slug.nodes.jsonl\"\r\n  49:         if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $pigNodes)) {\r\n  50:             return [pscustomobject]@{ ok = $false; reason = \"pdfdig lane: classified nodes missing beside the envelope ($slug.nodes.jsonl in the pig run dir) — run the pig orchestrator (Invoke-Pdfdig) / pdfdig-classify first\" }\r\n  51:         }\r\n  52:     }\r\n  53: \r\n  54:     # every invocation is a NEW run; prior runs are preserved untouched, by construction. But the new\r\n  55:     # run becomes the paper's current view — if the run it displaces carries agent work, say so loudly.\r\n  56:     $prior = @(Get-RunChunks $paperDir $slug)\r\n  57:     $displaced = $null\r\n  58:     if ($prior.Count) {\r\n  59:         $pStage = try { (Get-LedgerStage $prior[0]).stage } catch { $null }\r\n  60:         if ($pStage -and $pStage -ne 'preprocessed') {\r\n  61:             $displaced = \"prior run '$(Get-RunName $prior[0])' carries '$pStage' work — it stays intact; address it as $slug@$(Get-RunName $prior[0])\"\r\n  62:         }\r\n  63:     }\r\n  64:     $scratch = New-RunDir $paperDir\r\n  65:     $chunks  = Join-Path $scratch \"$slug.chunks.jsonl\"\r\n  66:     $nodes   = Join-Path $scratch \"$slug.nodes.jsonl\"\r\n  67: \r\n  68:     if ($lane -eq 'pdfdig') {\r\n  69:         # born signals in, compensation out: headings arrive pre-typed (typography + outline\r\n  70:         # cross-derivation), so docling-damage heading recovery is skipped on this lane\r\n  71:         Invoke-ProjectPdfDigNodes -PdfDigNodesPath $pigNodes -OutputPath $nodes -SourcePath $JsonPath | Out-Null\r\n  72:     } else {\r\n  73:         Invoke-ProjectIr       -JsonPath $JsonPath -OutputPath $nodes | Out-Null\r\n  74:         Invoke-HeadingRecovery -NodesPath $nodes | Out-Null\r\n  75:     }\r\n  76:     Invoke-Collapse        -NodesPath $nodes -OutputPath $chunks | Out-Null\r\n  77:     Invoke-Zones           -ChunksPath $chunks -NodesPath $nodes | Out-Null\r\n  78:     Invoke-Sections        -ChunksPath $chunks -NodesPath $nodes | Out-Null\r\n  79:     Invoke-Normalize       -ChunksPath $chunks -NodesPath $nodes -Lane $lane | Out-Null\r\n  80:     Invoke-Fidelity        -ChunksPath $chunks -NodesPath $nodes | Out-Null\r\n  81:     Invoke-Repair          -ChunksPath $chunks -NodesPath $nodes | Out-Null\r\n  82: \r\n  83:     $c = @(Read-Chunks $chunks)\r\n  84:     $tally = @{\r\n  85:         repaired     = @($c | Where-Object { $_.fidelity -eq 'repaired' }).Count\r\n  86:         needs_review = @($c | Where-Object { $_.fidelity -eq 'needs_review' }).Count\r\n  87:         needs_repair = @($c | Where-Object { $_.fidelity -eq 'needs_repair' }).Count\r\n  88:     }\r\n  89:     Add-LedgerEntry $chunks 'preprocessed' @{ repaired = $tally.repaired; needs_review = $tally.needs_review; needs_repair = $tally.needs_repair; ir_lane = $lane }\r\n  90: \r\n  91:     $out = [ordered]@{ ok = $true; paper = $slug; run = (Get-RunName $chunks); chunks = $c.Count; tally = $tally; path = $chunks; prior_runs = $prior.Count; ir_lane = $lane }\r\n  92:     if ($lane -eq 'pdfdig') {\r\n  93:         # apprise the operating agent: what this lane already did, and what it means downstream\r\n  94:         $out.lane_notes = 'pdfdig IR: headings arrive PRE-typed from born typography + PDF outline cross-derivation (heading recovery was skipped; tier/outline provenance in the {slug}.classify.json sidecar in the pig run dir, .runs/{stamp}/pig/); inline math carries $-seams with geometric sub/superscripts; formula chunks are grouped display-math lines (2-D assembly pending — needs_2d_assembly flags mark stacked groups); page furniture was dropped at the adapter (orientation/margin evidence); ligatures + symbol-map corrections are already applied. Node flags[] are dispatchable uncertainty markers from the converter, not detected corruption.'\r\n  95:     }\r\n  96:     if ($displaced) { $out.displaced = $displaced }\r\n  97:     [pscustomobject]$out\r\n  98: }\r\n===== src/codex-membrane/serving.ps1 =====\r\n   1: #requires -Version 7.0\r\n   2: <#\r\n   3:   src/codex-membrane/serving.ps1 — serving layer over the enriched chunk-JSONL.\r\n   4: \r\n   5:   The membrane: orchestrator-facing tools read metadata only (body-blind, so a\r\n   6:   50-page doc costs a few hundred tokens), and the sub-agent-facing slice tool\r\n   7:   returns exactly one work-unit by id via the .jidx seek (a worker never loads\r\n   8:   more than its slice + the context it explicitly asks for).\r\n   9: \r\n  10:   The write-side closes the loop, one chunk at a time (one proposal file per id, so\r\n  11:   concurrent workers never conflict). Add-RepairEdit is the pointed path — a surgical\r\n  12:   find->replace that never regenerates the chunk (anti-leakage); Add-RepairProposal is the\r\n  13:   wholesale fallback for anchorless corruption. The hard gate is apply: Invoke-RepairApply\r\n  14:   folds only clean staged content into the stream (Get-CorruptionType is the gate), keeps\r\n  15:   still-flagged proposals staged for more editing, clears the leases it merged, and writes a\r\n  16:   before/after audit. (apply is NOT a git commit.)\r\n  17: \r\n  18:     . ./serving.ps1\r\n  19:     Get-IrSummary       -ChunksPath <chunks.jsonl>\r\n  20:     Get-IrHotspots      -ChunksPath <chunks.jsonl> [-Type intertext]\r\n  21:     Get-Slice           -ChunksPath <chunks.jsonl> -Id <n> [-Context 1]\r\n  22:     Add-RepairEdit      -ChunksPath <chunks.jsonl> -Id <n> -Find <str> -Replace <str> [-Source <who>]\r\n  23:     Add-RepairProposal  -ChunksPath <chunks.jsonl> -Id <n> -Content <repaired> [-Source <who>]\r\n  24:     Invoke-RepairApply  -ChunksPath <chunks.jsonl> [-NodesPath <nodes.jsonl>]\r\n  25: #>\r\n  26: \r\n  27: . \"$PSScriptRoot/../jsonl.ps1\"\r\n  28: . \"$PSScriptRoot/fidelity.ps1\"\r\n  29: . \"$PSScriptRoot/playbook.ps1\"   # the repair recipes-as-data the work-order composer pools\r\n  30: . \"$PSScriptRoot/../crawl.ps1\"\r\n  31: . \"$PSScriptRoot/../runs.ps1\"       # run layout ({paper}/.runs/{stamp}) + {paper}@{run} addressing\r\n  32: . \"$PSScriptRoot/normalize.ps1\"\r\n  33: . \"$PSScriptRoot/../enrichment.ps1\"\r\n  34: . \"$PSScriptRoot/../pdf-converter/math-evidence.ps1\"   # Get-ChunkMathEvidence: geometry -> slice payload for gated math repair\r\n  35: \r\n  36: function Read-Chunks([string]$Path) {\r\n  37:     [System.IO.File]::ReadLines($Path) | Where-Object { $_ } | ForEach-Object { $_ | ConvertFrom-Json }\r\n  38: }\r\n  39: \r\n  40: # agreement (Part A): a chunk's structural-ambiguity score for dispatch RANKING. Absent ⇒ 1.0 (nothing\r\n  41: # disputed, lowest priority). fidelity.ps1 computes/stores it; here we only read it for ordering + surfacing.\r\n  42: function Get-ChunkAgreement($Chunk) {\r\n  43:     $v = $Chunk.agreement\r\n  44:     if ($null -ne $v) { return [double]$v }\r\n  45:     return 1.0\r\n  46: }\r\n  47: \r\n  48: # run layout + paper addressing live in runs.ps1 (shared with non-membrane lanes, e.g. the LaTeX\r\n  49: # converter's tarball unpacking) — sourced below with the other layers.\r\n  50: \r\n  51: # --- discovery over the per-source run layout (crawler, not -Recurse) ---\r\n  52: # ONE current view per paper: the newest run's chunks.\r\n  53: function Get-ChunkFiles([string]$Root) {\r\n  54:     $all = @(Invoke-Crawl -Root $Root -Patterns '**/.runs/*/*.chunks.jsonl' -Semantics Include)\r\n  55:     $seen = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)\r\n  56:     foreach ($cp in $all) {\r\n  57:         $paperDir = Get-PaperDirFromChunks $cp\r\n  58:         $slug     = (Split-Path -Leaf $cp) -replace '\\.chunks\\.jsonl$', ''\r\n  59:         if ($seen.Add(\"$paperDir|$slug\")) { Get-LatestChunks $paperDir $slug }\r\n  60:     }\r\n  61: }\r\n  62: \r\n  63: # survey the ingestion target: each paper raw + whether it's been preprocessed. A paper may carry\r\n  64: # one or both IR lanes — {slug}/{slug}.json (opendataloader/docling era) and/or\r\n  65: # {slug}/{slug}.pdfdig.json (the pdfdig converter's envelope) — aggregated into one row with a\r\n  66: # `lanes` field so the agent can see what intake dialects exist and pick one at preprocess.\r\n  67: function Get-IngestionScan([string]$Root) {\r\n  68:     $papers = [ordered]@{}\r\n  69:     # opendataloader/docling raws: {slug}/{slug}.json beside the source. (A retired beside-source\r\n  70:     # {slug}.pdfdig.json still matches here and is picked up as the pdfdig lane.)\r\n  71:     foreach ($json in (Invoke-Crawl -Root $Root -Patterns '**/*.json' -Semantics Include)) {\r\n  72:         $base = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($json)\r\n  73:         $lane = 'opendataloader'; $slug = $base\r\n  74:         if ($base.EndsWith('.pdfdig')) { $lane = 'pdfdig'; $slug = $base.Substring(0, $base.Length - 7) }\r\n  75:         $paperDir = Split-Path -Parent $json\r\n  76:         if ((Split-Path -Leaf $paperDir) -ne $slug) { continue }   # only {slug}/{slug}[.pdfdig].json raws (skips inventory.json etc.)\r\n  77:         $key = \"$paperDir|$slug\"\r\n  78:         if (-not $papers.Contains($key)) {\r\n  79:             $papers[$key] = @{ slug = $slug; dir = $paperDir; lanes = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new(); src = @{} }\r\n  80:         }\r\n  81:         if (-not $papers[$key].lanes.Contains($lane)) { $papers[$key].lanes.Add($lane) }\r\n  82:         $papers[$key].src[$lane] = $json\r\n  83:     }\r\n  84:     # pig lane: the pdfdig envelope now lives under {slug}/.runs/{stamp}/pig/ (git-ignored), not\r\n  85:     # beside the source. Detect a paper as pig-convertible from its newest such run, climbing out to\r\n  86:     # the real paper dir so it aggregates into the same row as any beside-source docling raw.\r\n  87:     foreach ($env in (Invoke-Crawl -Root $Root -Patterns '**/.runs/*/pig/*.pdfdig.json' -Semantics Include)) {\r\n  88:         $slug = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($env)\r\n  89:         $slug = $slug.Substring(0, $slug.Length - 7)   # strip trailing '.pdfdig' (GetFileNameWithoutExtension drops only '.json')\r\n  90:         $paperDir = Get-PaperDirFromIr $env\r\n  91:         if ((Split-Path -Leaf $paperDir) -ne $slug) { continue }   # only {slug}/.runs/*/pig/{slug}.pdfdig.json\r\n  92:         $key = \"$paperDir|$slug\"\r\n  93:         if (-not $papers.Contains($key)) {\r\n  94:             $papers[$key] = @{ slug = $slug; dir = $paperDir; lanes = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new(); src = @{} }\r\n  95:         }\r\n  96:         if (-not $papers[$key].lanes.Contains('pdfdig')) { $papers[$key].lanes.Add('pdfdig') }\r\n  97:         $papers[$key].src['pdfdig'] = (Get-PigEnvelope $paperDir $slug)   # newest run wins\r\n  98:     }\r\n  99:     foreach ($key in $papers.Keys) {\r\n 100:         $p = $papers[$key]\r\n 101:         $runs    = @(Get-RunChunks $p.dir $p.slug)\r\n 102:         $chunks  = if ($runs.Count) { $runs[0] } else { $null }\r\n 103:         $prepped = [bool]$chunks\r\n 104:         $stage = $null\r\n 105:         # Fault isolation: a corrupt ledger flags this one unit 'unreadable' instead of aborting the\r\n 106:         # whole survey (one bad unit must not blind the agent to every healthy one in the batch).\r\n 107:         if ($prepped) { try { $stage = (Get-LedgerStage $chunks).stage } catch { $stage = 'unreadable' } }\r\n 108:         $srcPath = if ($p.src.ContainsKey('opendataloader')) { $p.src['opendataloader'] } else { $p.src['pdfdig'] }\r\n 109:         [pscustomobject]@{\r\n 110:             paper      = $p.slug\r\n 111:             source     = ([System.IO.Path]::GetRelativePath($Root, $srcPath) -replace '\\\\', '/')\r\n 112:             lanes      = @($p.lanes | Sort-Object)\r\n 113:             prepped    = $prepped\r\n 114:             stage      = $stage\r\n 115:             runs       = $runs.Count\r\n 116:             latest_run = if ($chunks) { Get-RunName $chunks } else { $null }   # pin any run as {paper}@{run}\r\n 117:         }\r\n 118:     }\r\n 119: }\r\n 120: \r\n===== src/codex-membrane/project-ir.ps1 =====\r\n   1: #requires -Version 7.0\r\n   2: <#\r\n   3:   src/codex-membrane/project-ir.ps1 — project a Docling / opendataloader JSON IR into ordered node-JSONL.\r\n   4: \r\n   5:   Walks the nested struct tree, lifts every typed node into a flat record in\r\n   6:   document order, and emits node-JSONL + .jidx + .sig through the jsonl substrate.\r\n   7: \r\n   8:   Schema-aware: canonical fields are resolved through an alias map (discover the\r\n   9:   source key, don't assume it), and the distinct raw keys seen are reported — so an\r\n  10:   opendataloader schema change surfaces as a missing alias rather than a silent null.\r\n  11: \r\n  12:     . ./project-ir.ps1\r\n  13:     Invoke-ProjectIr -JsonPath <docling.json> -OutputPath <nodes.jsonl>\r\n  14: #>\r\n  15: \r\n  16: . \"$PSScriptRoot/../jsonl.ps1\"\r\n  17: \r\n  18: # canonical field  <-  candidate source keys (first present wins)\r\n  19: $script:CanonicalKeys = [ordered]@{\r\n  20:     page          = @('page number', 'page', 'pageNumber')\r\n  21:     level         = @('level')\r\n  22:     heading_level = @('heading level', 'heading_level')\r\n  23:     font          = @('font')\r\n  24:     font_size     = @('font size', 'font_size')\r\n  25:     bbox          = @('bounding box', 'bbox')\r\n  26:     content       = @('content', 'text')\r\n  27: }\r\n  28: \r\n  29: function Resolve-CanonicalField($Node, $Candidates) {\r\n  30:     foreach ($c in $Candidates) {\r\n  31:         $p = $Node.PSObject.Properties[$c]\r\n  32:         if ($null -ne $p) { return $p.Value }\r\n  33:     }\r\n  34:     return $null\r\n  35: }\r\n  36: \r\n  37: function Add-IrNodes {\r\n  38:     param(\r\n  39:         $Node,\r\n  40:         [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]   $Nodes,\r\n  41:         [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]] $RawKeys\r\n  42:     )\r\n  43:     if ($Node -is [string]) { return }\r\n  44:     if ($Node -is [System.Collections.IEnumerable]) {\r\n  45:         foreach ($i in $Node) { Add-IrNodes -Node $i -Nodes $Nodes -RawKeys $RawKeys }\r\n  46:         return\r\n  47:     }\r\n  48:     if ($Node -is [System.Management.Automation.PSCustomObject]) {\r\n  49:         if ($null -ne $Node.PSObject.Properties['type']) {\r\n  50:             foreach ($p in $Node.PSObject.Properties) { [void]$RawKeys.Add($p.Name) }\r\n  51:             $rec = [ordered]@{ id = $Nodes.Count; type = [string]$Node.type }\r\n  52:             foreach ($ck in $script:CanonicalKeys.Keys) {\r\n  53:                 $rec[$ck] = Resolve-CanonicalField $Node $script:CanonicalKeys[$ck]\r\n  54:             }\r\n  55:             $Nodes.Add([pscustomobject]$rec)\r\n  56:         }\r\n  57:         foreach ($p in $Node.PSObject.Properties) {\r\n  58:             Add-IrNodes -Node $p.Value -Nodes $Nodes -RawKeys $RawKeys\r\n  59:         }\r\n  60:     }\r\n  61: }\r\n  62: \r\n  63: function Invoke-ProjectIr {\r\n  64:     [CmdletBinding()]\r\n  65:     param(\r\n  66:         [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $JsonPath,\r\n  67:         [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $OutputPath\r\n  68:     )\r\n  69: \r\n  70:     $doc     = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllText($JsonPath, [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)) | ConvertFrom-Json   # .NET read: BOM-tolerant decode, no provider encoding ambiguity on external IR\r\n  71:     $nodes   = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()\r\n  72:     $rawKeys = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new()\r\n  73: \r\n  74:     Add-IrNodes -Node $doc -Nodes $nodes -RawKeys $rawKeys\r\n  75: \r\n  76:     $manifest = Write-JsonlStage -Records $nodes.ToArray() -OutputPath $OutputPath `\r\n  77:                                  -SourcePath $JsonPath -Stage 'project-ir'\r\n  78: \r\n  79:     \"$($nodes.Count) nodes -> $OutputPath  (+ .jidx, .sig)\"\r\n  80:     \"raw keys seen: $(($rawKeys | Sort-Object) -join ', ')\"\r\n  81:     \"--- canonical schema (coverage) ---\"\r\n  82:     Get-JsonlSchema -Path $OutputPath | Format-Table -AutoSize\r\n  83:     return $manifest\r\n  84: }\r\n===== src/codex-membrane/collapse.ps1 =====\r\n   1: #requires -Version 7.0\r\n   2: <#\r\n   3:   src/codex-membrane/collapse.ps1 — collapse node-JSONL (fragmented IR shards) into chunk-JSONL.\r\n   4: \r\n   5:   Walks the IR-ordered nodes and agglomerates consecutive prose shards into\r\n   6:   coherent chunks by bounding-box continuity, repairing inline as it goes. Figure\r\n   7:   debris (shards inside an image's padded bbox) is routed to a discards sidecar —\r\n   8:   nothing is dropped silently; kept chunks + discards = every input node.\r\n   9: \r\n  10:   Emits chunks.jsonl and discards.jsonl, each with coordinated .jidx + .sig.\r\n  11: \r\n  12:     . ./collapse.ps1\r\n  13:     Invoke-Collapse -NodesPath <nodes.jsonl> -OutputPath <chunks.jsonl>\r\n  14: \r\n  15:   Merge model (bbox = [x0,y0,x1,y1], PDF points, y-up; top = y1), vs the previous shard:\r\n  16:     same line  (|Δtop| < 0.5·lh):  concatenate; space iff the x-gap is a word gap\r\n  17:     next line  (0.5·lh ≤ Δtop ≤ 1.8·lh): join with a space (trailing hyphen joins tight)\r\n  18:     otherwise  (bigger gap / page change): close the chunk\r\n  19:   Structural nodes (heading/formula/image/…) flush the open prose chunk and emit their own.\r\n  20: #>\r\n  21: \r\n  22: . \"$PSScriptRoot/../jsonl.ps1\"\r\n  23: \r\n  24: $script:Ligatures = @{ 'ﬁ' = 'fi'; 'ﬂ' = 'fl'; 'ﬃ' = 'ffi'; 'ﬀ' = 'ff'; 'ﬄ' = 'ffl' }\r\n  25: \r\n  26: function Remove-Ligatures([string]$s) {\r\n  27:     foreach ($k in $script:Ligatures.Keys) {\r\n  28:         if ($s.Contains($k)) { $s = $s.Replace($k, $script:Ligatures[$k]) }\r\n  29:     }\r\n  30:     return $s\r\n  31: }\r\n  32: \r\n  33: function Merge-Bbox($a, $b) {\r\n  34:     return @([Math]::Min($a[0], $b[0]), [Math]::Min($a[1], $b[1]),\r\n  35:              [Math]::Max($a[2], $b[2]), [Math]::Max($a[3], $b[3]))\r\n  36: }\r\n  37: \r\n  38: function Get-ImageBoxesByPage($Nodes, [double]$Margin) {\r\n  39:     $boxes = @{}\r\n  40:     foreach ($n in $Nodes) {\r\n  41:         if ($n.type -ne 'image') { continue }\r\n  42:         $b = $n.bbox\r\n  43:         if (-not $b -or $b.Count -ne 4) { continue }\r\n  44:         $x0 = [double]$b[0]; $y0 = [double]$b[1]; $x1 = [double]$b[2]; $y1 = [double]$b[3]\r\n  45:         if (-not $boxes.ContainsKey($n.page)) { $boxes[$n.page] = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new() }\r\n  46:         $boxes[$n.page].Add(@(($x0 - $Margin), ($y0 - $Margin), ($x1 + $Margin), ($y1 + $Margin)))\r\n  47:     }\r\n  48:     return $boxes\r\n  49: }\r\n  50: \r\n  51: function Test-InsideAny($Bbox, $Boxes) {\r\n  52:     if (-not $Boxes) { return $false }\r\n  53:     $cx = ($Bbox[0] + $Bbox[2]) / 2.0\r\n  54:     $cy = ($Bbox[1] + $Bbox[3]) / 2.0\r\n  55:     foreach ($bx in $Boxes) {\r\n  56:         if ($bx[0] -le $cx -and $cx -le $bx[2] -and $bx[1] -le $cy -and $cy -le $bx[3]) { return $true }\r\n  57:     }\r\n  58:     return $false\r\n  59: }\r\n  60: \r\n  61: function Invoke-Collapse {\r\n  62:     [CmdletBinding()]\r\n  63:     param(\r\n  64:         [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $NodesPath,\r\n  65:         [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $OutputPath\r\n  66:     )\r\n  67: \r\n  68:     $nodes = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()\r\n  69:     foreach ($line in $n.bbox[1]) }\r\n  76:     }\r\n  77:     $lh = if ($heights.Count) { ($heights | Sort-Object)[[int][math]::Floor($heights.Count / 2)] } else { 10.0 }\r\n  78: \r\n  79:     $imageBoxes = Get-ImageBoxesByPage $nodes (1.5 * $lh)\r\n  80: \r\n  81:     $chunks   = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()\r\n  82:     $discards = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()\r\n  83:     $cur = $null\r\n  84:     $lastTop = 0.0\r\n  85:     $lastX1 = 0.0\r\n  86: \r\n  87:     foreach ($nd in $nodes) {\r\n  88:         $t = $nd.type\r\n  89:         $bbox = $nd.bbox\r\n  90:         $content = Remove-Ligatures ([string]$nd.content)\r\n  91:         $hasBbox = ($bbox -and $bbox.Count -eq 4)\r\n  92: \r\n  93:         if ($t -eq 'paragraph' -and $hasBbox -and (Test-InsideAny $bbox $imageBoxes[$nd.page])) {\r\n  94:             if ($cur) { $chunks.Add($cur); $cur = $null }\r\n  95:             $discards.Add([pscustomobject][ordered]@{\r\n  96:                 id = $nd.id; type = $t; page = $nd.page; bbox = $bbox; content = $content\r\n  97:                 discard_reason = 'figure_debris'; discard_pass = 'collapse'\r\n  98:             })\r\n  99:             continue\r\n 100:         }\r\n 101: \r\n 102:         if ($t -eq 'paragraph' -and $hasBbox) {\r\n 103:             $ntop = $bbox[3]; $nx0 = $bbox[0]; $nx1 = $bbox[2]\r\n 104:             if ($cur -and $nd.page -eq $cur.page) {\r\n 105:                 $dtop = $lastTop - $ntop\r\n 106:                 if ([math]::Abs($ntop - $lastTop) -lt 0.5 * $lh) {\r\n 107:                     $sep = if (($nx0 - $lastX1) -gt 0.25 * $lh) { ' ' } else { '' }\r\n 108:                     $cur.content += $sep + $content\r\n 109:                     $cur.bbox = Merge-Bbox $cur.bbox $bbox\r\n 110:                     $cur.n_shards++\r\n 111:                     $lastTop = $ntop; $lastX1 = $nx1\r\n 112:                     continue\r\n 113:                 }\r\n 114:                 if ($dtop -ge 0.5 * $lh -and $dtop -le 1.8 * $lh) {\r\n 115:                     # line-break join. A trailing hyphen before a lowercase continuation is a\r\n 116:                     # word-wrap soft hyphen (Clas-/sical) → strip it. BUT a genuine compound can wrap\r\n 117:                     # at its own hyphen (delta-/homology); we can't tell without a lexicon, so we\r\n 118:                     # dehyphenate best-effort and FLAG the chunk for the enrichment tier to verify.\r\n 119:                     if ($cur.content.EndsWith('-') -and $content -match '^[a-z]') {\r\n 120:                         $cur.content = $cur.content.Substring(0, $cur.content.Length - 1) + $content\r\n===== src/finalize.ps1 =====\r\n   1: #requires -Version 7.0\r\n   2: <#\r\n   3:   src/finalize.ps1 — serialize the repaired chunk stream into the corpus deliverable.\r\n   4: \r\n   5:   Walks the enriched chunks in reading order and emits codex-scientiae markdown per\r\n   6:   STANDARDS.md: an H1 title, a `## Contents` block, body sections at H2/H3/H4 by depth, prose\r\n   7:   paragraphs, block math fenced in $$, and running-head furniture dropped. The back-matter\r\n   8:   (References) is split into a sidecar references/{slug}.md, linked from Contents. First pass\r\n   9:   writes into the document's own run dir (.runs/{stamp}/) — get the SHAPE right;\r\n  10:   the move to compendia/{topic}/ is a later concern. Logs the 'finalized' milestone.\r\n  11: \r\n  12:     . ./finalize.ps1\r\n  13:     Invoke-Finalize -ChunksPath <chunks.jsonl> [-OutputDir <dir>]\r\n  14: #>\r\n  15: \r\n  16: . \"$PSScriptRoot/codex-membrane/serving.ps1\"\r\n  17: . \"$PSScriptRoot/runs.ps1\"          # Get-PigRunDirs (newest-wins) — the figure weave reads the pig lane\r\n  18: . \"$PSScriptRoot/audits/md-register.ps1\"   # the ONE markdown figure register, shared with the LaTeX oracle lane\r\n  19: . \"$PSScriptRoot/audits/md-toc.ps1\"        # the ONE heading-slug engine + Contents-block builder (Get-MdAnchor)\r\n  20: \r\n  21: # caption furniture -> italic, heading -> #*(level+1), block formula -> $$ fence, else content as-is\r\n  22: function Format-Chunk($c) {\r\n  23:     if ([string]$c.is_furniture -eq 'caption') { return '*' + ([string]$c.content) + '*' }\r\n  24:     switch ([string]$c.type) {\r\n  25:         'heading' { $lvl = if ($c.section_level) { [Math]::Min(6, [int]$c.section_level + 1) } else { 2 }; ('#' * $lvl) + ' ' + ([string]$c.content) }\r\n  26:         'formula' { '$$' + \"`n\" + ([string]$c.content) + \"`n\" + '$$' }\r\n  27:         default   { [string]$c.content }\r\n  28:     }\r\n  29: }\r\n  30: \r\n  31: # ── caption relocation — reunite a shattered caption with its figure's in-text anchor ──────────────\r\n  32: # The caption's own figure/table handle: the leading \"Fig. 1\" / \"Table 3\" a caption furniture chunk\r\n  33: # opens with (the SAME shape normalize's Get-FurnitureKind gates on). Returns { kind; num } — kind\r\n  34: # normalized to 'figure'/'table' so a \"Fig.\" caption anchors to a \"Figure 1\" reference — or $null when\r\n  35: # the chunk is not a caption / carries no leading numbered label (leave it exactly where it is).\r\n  36: function Get-CaptionLabel($c) {\r\n  37:     if ([string]$c.is_furniture -ne 'caption') { return $null }\r\n  38:     $m = [regex]::Match(([string]$c.content).Trim(), '^(Figure|Fig\\.?|Table|Tab\\.?)\\s*(\\d+)', 'IgnoreCase')\r\n  39:     if (-not $m.Success) { return $null }\r\n  40:     $kind = if ($m.Groups[1].Value -match '^(?i:fig)') { 'figure' } else { 'table' }\r\n  41:     return [pscustomobject]@{ kind = $kind; num = $m.Groups[2].Value }\r\n  42: }\r\n  43: \r\n  44: # Does a body chunk carry an in-text mention of (kind num) — \"Figure 1\", \"Fig. 1\", \"(Figure 1 ,\",\r\n  45: # \"see Fig. 6\", \"shown in Table 3\"? CASE-SENSITIVE (real references are capitalized) so a lowercase\r\n  46: # \"table\"/\"figure\" prose word is never a false anchor; word-anchored + digit-bounded so \"Figure 1\"\r\n  47: # never matches \"Figure 10\"/\"Figure 12\".\r\n  48: function Test-FigureReference($c, $Label) {\r\n  49:     $verb = if ($Label.kind -eq 'figure') { '(?:Figure|Fig\\.?)' } else { '(?:Table|Tab\\.?)' }\r\n  50:     $rx = '(?<![A-Za-z])' + $verb + '\\s*' + [regex]::Escape($Label.num) + '(?![0-9])'\r\n  51:     return [regex]::IsMatch([string]$c.content, $rx)\r\n  52: }\r\n  53: \r\n  54: # Docling frequently shatters a FIGURE caption away from its figure and drops it mid-prose; normalize.ps1\r\n  55: # CLASSIFIES the stray as is_furniture='caption' but leaves it in place, so it interrupts the body flow.\r\n  56: # Here — at EMISSION only, never touching the persisted chunk stream or its id==line-number seek\r\n  57: # invariant — relocate each figure caption to sit immediately after the FIRST body chunk that references\r\n  58: # its figure number in-text (the anchor the paper's own prose gives, and the exact spot the publish/splice\r\n  59: # tier later weaves the figure pixels into — preprocess strips images, so the caption is what's orphaned).\r\n  60: # A caption whose number is nowhere referenced in the body stays exactly where it was — never lost, never\r\n  61: # mis-placed. Pure list transform over an unchanging input: recomputes the same order every run, so a\r\n  62: # second pass is a no-op (idempotent).\r\n  63: #\r\n  64: # FIGURE captions only — deliberately NOT tables. The image-stripping \"reunite the orphan with its splice\r\n  65: # point\" rationale is figure-specific (a table's own cells are not stripped, so its caption is not orphaned\r\n  66: # the same way), and a table's \"Tab. N\"/\"Table N\" cue collides with bibliographic citations of OTHER works'\r\n  67: # tables (\"Vinh et al , 2010 , Tab. 2\") — anchoring on those would mis-place the caption. Table captions\r\n  68: # stay in reading order rather than ride a reference signal that can't tell a cross-cite from a real anchor.\r\n  69: function Move-CaptionsToAnchors($BodyChunks) {\r\n  70:     $items = @($BodyChunks)\r\n  71:     # capIndex -> anchor chunk id it should trail (only figure captions with a resolvable in-text reference)\r\n  72:     $anchorId = @{}\r\n  73:     for ($i = 0; $i -lt $items.Count; $i++) {\r\n  74:         $label = Get-CaptionLabel $items[$i]\r\n  75:         if (-not $label -or $label.kind -ne 'figure') { continue }   # figure captions only (see note above)\r\n  76:         for ($j = 0; $j -lt $items.Count; $j++) {\r\n  77:             if ($j -eq $i -or [string]$items[$j].is_furniture -eq 'caption') { continue }   # anchors are real body prose, never another caption\r\n  78:             if (Test-FigureReference $items[$j] $label) { $anchorId[$i] = [int]$items[$j].id; break }\r\n  79:         }\r\n  80:     }\r\n  81:     if ($anchorId.Count -eq 0) { return $items }\r\n  82:     # captions to inject after each anchor id, keyed by anchor id, in stable original-body order\r\n  83:     $trailing = @{}\r\n  84:     foreach ($ci in ($anchorId.Keys | Sort-Object)) {\r\n  85:         $aid = $anchorId[$ci]\r\n  86:         if (-not $trailing.ContainsKey($aid)) { $trailing[$aid] = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new() }\r\n  87:         $trailing[$aid].Add($items[$ci])\r\n  88:     }\r\n  89:     $out = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()\r\n  90:     for ($i = 0; $i -lt $items.Count; $i++) {\r\n  91:         if ($anchorId.ContainsKey($i)) { continue }                    # a relocated caption — emitted after its anchor below\r\n  92:         $out.Add($items[$i])\r\n  93:         if ($trailing.ContainsKey([int]$items[$i].id)) {\r\n  94:             foreach ($cap in $trailing[[int]$items[$i].id]) { $out.Add($cap) }\r\n  95:         }\r\n  96:     }\r\n  97:     return $out.ToArray()\r\n  98: }\r\n  99: \r\n 100: # ── figure weave — the finalized markdown drinks the pig figure lane ────────────────────────────────\r\n 101: # The measurement marginal: every kind=figure region of the paper's NEWEST pig run enters the emitted\r\n 102: # body as an image line through the SAME register the LaTeX oracle emits (md-register.ps1) — best-effort\r\n 103: # BY DESIGN. Rendering is deliberately indifferent to detection quality: if the figure lane is wrong,\r\n 104: # the markdown shows it, and that visibility is the instrument. Placement: a CAPTIONED region rides its\r\n 105: # caption chunk (wherever Move-CaptionsToAnchors put it — the caption is the placement token this\r\n 106: # architecture reserved for exactly this weave); an UNCAPTIONED region (inline diagrams + residue)\r\n 107: # flushes when the reading order leaves its page. A region whose crop failed emits the flagged marker —\r\n 108: # nothing silent. Crop PNGs copy into {OutputDir}/{slug}-membrane/ (lane-infixed: never collides with\r\n 109: # the oracle's {slug}/ image dir; the paper-root mirror's links resolve once publish carries the dir up).\r\n 110: # Returns $null when the paper has no pig run / figure lane (e.g. pure docling papers).\r\n 111: function Get-FigureWeave([string]$PaperRoot, [string]$Slug, [string]$OutputDir) {\r\n 112:     $pigDirs = @(Get-PigRunDirs $PaperRoot $Slug)\r\n 113:     if (-not $pigDirs.Count) { return $null }\r\n 114:     $pig = $pigDirs[0]\r\n 115:     $figuresJsonl = Join-Path $pig \"$Slug.figures.jsonl\"\r\n 116:     $manifestPath = Join-Path $pig 'images.jsonl'\r\n 117:     if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $figuresJsonl) -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $manifestPath)) { return $null }\r\n 118: \r\n 119:     $crop = @{}\r\n 120:     foreach ($line in [System.IO.File]::ReadLines($manifestPath)) {\r\n===== src/pdf-converter/pdfdig-ir.ps1 =====\r\n   1: #requires -Version 7.0\r\n   2: <#\r\n   3:   src/pdf-converter/pdfdig-ir.ps1 — pdfdig generic IR emitter.\r\n   4: \r\n   5:   Faithful, opinion-free projection of everything PdfPig can see into the multi-lane JSONL\r\n   6:   substrate described in issues/pdfdig-lane/ir-schema.md. NO classification: roles/scripts/columns\r\n   7:   are measured or recorded-as-claims, never decided here. See issues/pdfdig-lane/pdfpig-capability-map.md\r\n   8:   for the empirical basis of every choice below.\r\n   9: \r\n  10:   Lanes emitted (ir-schema.md build order 1-3):\r\n  11:     {slug}.pdfdig.json     document envelope (provenance, origin, bookmarks, font census, health)\r\n  12:     {slug}.letters.jsonl   LANE 1  atomic: every Letter, all born signals (+ block/line/word back-refs)\r\n  13:     {slug}.words.jsonl     LANE 2  derived: NearestNeighbour word assembly\r\n  14:     {slug}.blocks.jsonl    LANE 3  derived: RecursiveXYCut segmentation + reading order — a CLAIM lane\r\n  15:     {slug}.paths.jsonl     LANE 4  vector: paths w/ bezier command-point bbox fallback + rule tags\r\n  16: \r\n  17:     . ./pdfdig-ir.ps1\r\n  18:     ConvertTo-PdfDigIr -PdfPath <in.pdf> [-OutDir <dir>] [-Pages 1,2] [-Verbose]\r\n  19: #>\r\n  20: \r\n  21: # NB: no session-scope Set-StrictMode — this is a dot-sourceable library; forcing strict mode on\r\n  22: # callers pollutes their session (and trips the host's exit-code epilogue). Code below is strict-safe.\r\n  23: . \"$PSScriptRoot/../jsonl.ps1\"   # Write-JsonlStage: UTF-8-no-BOM, SMP-safe, .jidx + .sig\r\n  24: \r\n  25: $script:PdfPigLib = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'lib'   # vendored dlls; falls back to repo lib/pdfpig\r\n  26: if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $script:PdfPigLib 'UglyToad.PdfPig.dll'))) {\r\n  27:     $script:PdfPigLib = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '../../lib/pdfpig'\r\n  28: }\r\n  29: \r\n  30: # ── Interop: dependency-ordered load; nullable-struct + out-param traps live here once ──────────\r\n  31: function Import-PdfPig {\r\n  32:     [CmdletBinding()] param([string] $LibDir = $script:PdfPigLib)\r\n  33:     if ('UglyToad.PdfPig.PdfDocument' -as [type]) { return }   # idempotent\r\n  34:     $order = 'UglyToad.PdfPig.Tokens','UglyToad.PdfPig.Core','UglyToad.PdfPig.Tokenization',\r\n  35:              'UglyToad.PdfPig.Fonts','UglyToad.PdfPig','UglyToad.PdfPig.DocumentLayoutAnalysis'\r\n  36:     foreach ($n in $order) {\r\n  37:         $dll = Join-Path $LibDir \"$n.dll\"\r\n  38:         if (Test-Path $dll) { Add-Type -Path $dll }\r\n  39:         elseif ($n -notlike '*DocumentLayoutAnalysis') { throw \"PdfPig assembly not found: $dll\" }\r\n  40:     }\r\n  41: }\r\n  42: \r\n  43: # ── Config stores (rules-as-data): every cue the engine consults is a validated store, never code.\r\n  44: #    A malformed/incomplete entry THROWS with its line number — bad data is a failure, not a silent\r\n  45: #    skip. See stores/README.md + the growth loop. ─────────────────────────────────────────────────\r\n  46: function Read-JsonlStore([string] $Path, [string[]] $Required) {\r\n  47:     if (-not (Test-Path $Path)) { throw \"store not found: $Path\" }\r\n  48:     $name = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileName($Path)\r\n  49:     $rows = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()\r\n  50:     $ln = 0\r\n  51:     # ReadAllLines (eager) not ReadLines (lazy): a validation throw mid-file must not leave the handle open\r\n  52:     foreach ($line in [System.IO.File]::ReadAllLines($Path)) {\r\n  53:         $ln++\r\n  54:         if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($line)) { continue }\r\n  55:         $o = $null\r\n  56:         try { $o = $line | ConvertFrom-Json } catch { throw \"$name line ${ln}: bad JSON — $($_.Exception.Message)\" }\r\n  57:         foreach ($req in $Required) {\r\n  58:             if (-not $o.PSObject.Properties[$req] -or ($null -eq $o.$req) -or ($o.$req -is [string] -and $o.$req -eq '')) {\r\n  59:                 throw \"$name line ${ln}: missing required field '$req'\"\r\n  60:             }\r\n  61:         }\r\n  62:         $rows.Add($o)\r\n  63:     }\r\n  64:     return $rows\r\n  65: }\r\n  66: \r\n  67: $script:FontRoles = $null\r\n  68: function Import-FontRoles {\r\n  69:     [CmdletBinding()] param([string] $Path = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'stores/font-roles.jsonl'))\r\n  70:     $rows = foreach ($o in (Read-JsonlStore $Path @('pattern','role','family'))) {\r\n  71:         [pscustomobject]@{ pattern=$o.pattern\r\n  72:                            match=($o.PSObject.Properties['match'] ? $o.match : 'prefix')\r\n  73:                            role=$o.role; family=$o.family\r\n  74:                            domain=($o.PSObject.Properties['domain'] ? $o.domain : $null) }\r\n  75:     }\r\n  76:     # longest pattern first ⇒ most specific claim wins (CMMIB before CMMI, LMRomanCaps before LMRoman)\r\n  77:     $script:FontRoles = @($rows | Sort-Object { $_.pattern.Length } -Descending)\r\n  78:     $script:FontRoles.Count\r\n  79: }\r\n  80: \r\n  81: $script:ProducerMap = $null\r\n  82: function Import-ProducerMap {\r\n  83:     [CmdletBinding()] param([string] $Path = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'stores/producer-map.jsonl'))\r\n  84:     $rows = foreach ($o in (Read-JsonlStore $Path @('pattern','origin'))) {\r\n  85:         [pscustomobject]@{ pattern=$o.pattern; origin=$o.origin\r\n  86:                            tex=($o.PSObject.Properties['tex'] ? $o.tex : $null)          # true/false/null=inconclusive\r\n  87:                            rewriter=($o.PSObject.Properties['rewriter'] ? [bool]$o.rewriter : $false) }\r\n  88:     }\r\n  89:     $script:ProducerMap = @($rows | Sort-Object { $_.pattern.Length } -Descending)\r\n  90:     $script:ProducerMap.Count\r\n  91: }\r\n  92: \r\n  93: $script:ClassifyConfig = $null\r\n  94: $script:ClassifyConfigHash = $null\r\n  95: function Import-ClassifyConfig {\r\n  96:     [CmdletBinding()] param([string] $Path = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'stores/classify-config.json'))\r\n  97:     if (-not (Test-Path $Path)) { throw \"classify-config not found: $Path\" }\r\n  98:     $raw = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllText($Path, [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))\r\n  99:     $script:ClassifyConfig = $raw | ConvertFrom-Json\r\n 100:     # config_hash rides in the IR header so conversions are version-diffable against knob changes\r\n 101:     $sha = [System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256]::HashData([System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($raw))\r\n 102:     $script:ClassifyConfigHash = ([System.Convert]::ToHexString($sha)).Substring(0,12).ToLowerInvariant()\r\n 103:     $script:ClassifyConfigHash\r\n 104: }\r\n 105: \r\n 106: function Get-FontSubsetStripped([string] $name) {\r\n 107:     if (-not $name) { return '' }\r\n 108:     # subset tag is 6 chars + '+' (e.g. ASYHPE+NimbusRomNo9L-Regu)\r\n 109:     if ($name.Length -gt 7 -and $name[6] -eq '+') { return $name.Substring(7) }\r\n 110:     return $name\r\n 111: }\r\n 112: \r\n 113: function Resolve-Family([string] $strippedName) {\r\n 114:     if (-not $strippedName) { return @{ family='unknown'; role='unknown'; domain=$null } }\r\n 115:     if ($null -eq $script:FontRoles) { Import-FontRoles | Out-Null }\r\n 116:     foreach ($e in $script:FontRoles) {   # already sorted longest-first ⇒ first hit is most specific\r\n 117:         $hit = if ($e.match -eq 'prefix') {\r\n 118:             $strippedName.StartsWith($e.pattern, [StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)\r\n 119:         } else {\r\n 120:             $strippedName.IndexOf($e.pattern, [StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase) -ge 0\r\n===== src/pdf-converter/pdfdig-classify.ps1 =====\r\n   1: #requires -Version 7.0\r\n   2: <#\r\n   3:   src/pdf-converter/pdfdig-classify.ps1 — the pdfdig CLASSIFIER: typed node stream from the lanes.\r\n   4: \r\n   5:   Consumer of the generic IR substrate (pdfdig-ir.ps1). Where the substrate records measurements\r\n   6:   and claims, THIS stage forms opinions — every one calibrated from the document itself, sourced\r\n   7:   from the stores, and flagged when uncertain (flags, never guesses):\r\n   8: \r\n   9:     Stage A  CALIBRATION  per-document order statistics over the lanes: body size, heading tier\r\n  10:              ladder, modal leading, paragraph indent. > **Summarizing jsonl-v2 findings and target design**

I’ll treat these as one operational stack: run identity/layout, staged JSONL workflow, ledger/provenance, and logging. I’ll first map their callers and data flow, then separate reusable mechanics from application policy and identify overlap, compatibility seams, and migration order. I’m auditing only in this pass—no production edits.

The repository doesn’t have separate `jsonl-stage.ps1` or `run-ledger.ps1` files; both are currently embedded in [jsonl.ps1](D:/aghado01/codex-scientiae/src/shared/jsonl.ps1): `Write-JsonlStage` is the stage publisher and `Add/Get-Ledger*` is the ledger section. That confirms the coupling you remembered. I’m auditing those sections alongside `runs.ps1` and `log.ps1`, including their actual callers rather than treating the filenames as isolated libraries.

The live call graph is already revealing: `jsonl.ps1` has no tracked production importer, `Write-JsonlStage` has no production caller, and the only remaining ledger call is reached through a missing `codex-membrane/finalize.ps1` import. `runs.ps1` is active only through `latex-ingest`; the logger has tests but no production integration. I’m going into the recent history next so the reorganization preserves the intended workflow without treating retired membrane wiring as current architecture.

The architectural seam is now clear. The old membrane used these as an implicit coordinator: `New-RunDir` created a workspace, every transformation rewrote a canonical JSONL plus sidecars, the ledger supplied “current stage,” and inventory was silently updated as a writer side effect. The new `artifacts/{module}/runs/{stamp}/{slug}` convention retained only directory creation; it never gained an explicit run identity, manifest, completion boundary, or coordinator. The logger then independently reimplemented path resolution. I’m consolidating the audit into target boundaries and migration order now.

The audit confirms these are one operational system, but their responsibilities are currently tangled and most of the original system is retired residue rather than active infrastructure.

No files were changed during this audit.

## Current operational status

| Unit | Responsibilities currently mixed together | Live usage |
|---|---|---|
| [jsonl.ps1](D:/aghado01/codex-scientiae/src/shared/jsonl.ps1) | JSONL serialization, indexes, stage publication, provenance stamps, inventory, ledger, schema inspection | No tracked production importer; retained mainly by encoding tests |
| [runs.ps1](D:/aghado01/codex-scientiae/src/shared/runs.ps1) | Generic artifact roots, run allocation, legacy `.runs`, paper addressing, crawler-backed discovery, PdfPig compatibility | `latex-ingest` actively uses only its module-run and source-work helpers |
| [log.ps1](D:/aghado01/codex-scientiae/src/shared/log.ps1) | Run-log path resolution, run-context state, serialization, console policy, child-process inheritance, log querying | Tested but not integrated into production callers |
| Ledger section | Lifecycle milestones and current-stage projection | One lingering call from `publish.ps1`, reached through a currently missing membrane import |
| Inventory section | Best-effort artifact registry | Only invoked as a hidden `Write-JsonlStage` side effect |

Historically, the membrane orchestrator joined them like this:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R["New-RunDir"] --> S["Pipeline stages"]
    S --> J["Write-JsonlStage"]
    J --> A["JSONL + JIDX + SIG"]
    J --> I["inventory.json"]
    S --> L["ledger.jsonl"]
    L --> D["Latest/current-stage discovery"]
```

That orchestration disappeared during the source reorganization, but its storage assumptions remained in the shared files.

## Principal findings

### 1. `Write-JsonlStage` is not a reusable JSONL primitive

It silently truncates the destination through `StreamWriter(..., $false, ...)` at [jsonl.ps1:123](D:/aghado01/codex-scientiae/src/shared/jsonl.ps1:123). If serialization fails midway, the prior artifact is gone and the new artifact is partial.

Other problems:

- JSONL, index, signature, and inventory are published independently. There is no coordinated commit.
- Existing `.jidx`, `.sig`, and `inventory.json` files are silently replaced.
- Inventory failure is completely swallowed at [jsonl.ps1:170](D:/aghado01/codex-scientiae/src/shared/jsonl.ps1:170).
- Inventory uses an unlocked read-modify-write cycle, so concurrent registrations can be lost.
- It still emits `records.jsonl.jidx`.
- It claims LF output but never sets `StreamWriter.NewLine`; on Windows the stage writer emits CRLF.
- A `.sig` usually hashes `nodes.jsonl`, even when the actual transformation also consumed and replaced an existing `chunks.jsonl`. It therefore does not describe the complete input state.
- The `.sig` and inventory contain overlapping but incomplete projections of the same artifact event.

The generic mechanics belong in `jsonl-v2.ps1`. Stage publication should become a higher-level, explicit operation.

### 2. Run allocation is not concurrency-safe

Both run allocators use “check until unused, then create with `-Force`”:

- [New-ModuleRunDir](D:/aghado01/codex-scientiae/src/shared/runs.ps1:55)
- [New-RunDir](D:/aghado01/codex-scientiae/src/shared/runs.ps1:91)

Two processes can select the same candidate before either creates it, after which `-Force` lets them share the directory silently.

Additional run-layout problems:

- Discovery treats a directory or expected artifact as evidence that a run is usable. There is no `running/completed/failed` boundary, so newest-run selection can expose partial runs.
- Numeric collision suffixes stop sorting correctly lexically after `-9`.
- `Module` and `Slug` are used as path components without a clear validation contract.
- Explicit `-RunDir` silently reuses an existing directory in `latex-ingest`.
- Functions return bare path strings, forcing callers to rediscover run identity from path shape. This already produces a bug: [latex-ingest.ps1:2685](D:/aghado01/codex-scientiae/src/latex-ingest/latex-ingest.ps1:2685) reports the leaf—which is the slug—as `run`, not the runstamp.
- Generic module-run behavior is mixed with retired paper addressing, `.runs`, crawler, and PdfPig compatibility.

### 3. Ledger, inventory, provenance, and logging lack distinct authority

The old ledger describes itself as “one per document,” but its path is derived from run-local `chunks.jsonl`; it is actually one per document-run.

Its records have:

- no timestamp;
- no sequence or event identifier;
- no success/failure state;
- no schema identifier;
- no transition validation;
- no concurrency handling.

`Extra` can even replace the reserved `stage` field.

The conceptual separation should be:

- `run.json`: authoritative run identity and current lifecycle projection.
- `run-ledger.jsonl`: durable operational facts and transitions.
- `trace.jsonl`: best-effort diagnostic execution trace.
- Artifact inventory: a projection from ledger/manifest records, not another silently maintained mutable file.
- Provenance: part of artifact-publication ledger records, not one `.sig` beside every file.

This would eliminate both `inventory.json` and most `.sig` proliferation.

### 4. The logger currently violates the desired failure and file-count policies

At [log.ps1:153](D:/aghado01/codex-scientiae/src/shared/log.ps1:153), serialization or append failures propagate into the application. That means logging can:

- terminate a run;
- mask the original exception inside `Measure-RunStep`;
- leave `Stop-RunLog` incomplete.

Its child-process strategy deliberately creates `trace-{module}-{pid}.jsonl`, contradicting the revised requirement of one trace per run. The check for an existing `trace.jsonl` is also racy.

Other issues:

- It exports a directory rather than the exact shared log path.
- Exported environment state is not restored on stop.
- `-Force` abandons the old context without a closing record.
- Starting against an existing explicit path silently appends a new run to it.
- Invalid environment configuration silently falls back.
- Records do not carry run ID and PID consistently, which will matter when multiple processes share one trace.
- `AppendAllText` does not provide reliable multi-process record serialization.

The logger needs bounded contention handling through the JSONL primitive, a non-throwing emergency path to stderr, and recovery telemetry—but no alternate logfile sidecars.

## Recommended target structure

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Application adapter\ncaller-specific defaults"] --> C["Run coordinator"]
    C --> R["Run identity + layout"]
    C --> M["run.json lifecycle"]
    C --> L["Run ledger"]
    C --> G["One shared trace.jsonl"]
    C --> S["Stage/artifact publisher"]

    S --> J["JSONL primitives"]
    L --> J
    G --> J

    P["Paper/PdfPig/legacy discovery"] -. "application or compatibility layer" .-> A
```

### Shared JSONL substrate

`jsonl-v2.ps1` remains limited to:

- strict JSONL I/O;
- complete-file publication;
- safe append;
- validation;
- snapshots;
- optional indexes.

It must not know about stages, runs, logs, inventories, or provenance.

### Run identity and layout

A pending replacement should return a run-context object rather than a path:

```text
RunId
RunStamp
Application
Operation
Subject
ArtifactsRoot
RunRoot
RunDirectory
LogPath
LedgerPath
ManifestPath
StartedAt
```

Creation must claim the directory atomically. Existing explicit run directories should fail by default; reuse should require an explicit policy.

I recommend keeping Git commit, dirty state, source hashes, parameters, and full timestamps in `run.json`. The directory name should remain human-oriented rather than carrying all provenance.

### Run coordinator

A PowerShell equivalent of a decorator can be an `Invoke-WithRun` higher-order function:

```text
resolve application defaults from caller-bound parameters
→ allocate or join a run context
→ initialize manifest and ledger
→ start logger
→ execute caller body
→ record completed/failed result
→ stop logger in finally
```

Each application supplies defaults and layout policy. The generic coordinator does not guess what `latex-ingest`, procurement, or an MCP server considers a run.

### Stage publisher

A future stage utility should:

1. Call the JSONL complete-file primitive with explicit `Fail` or `Replace`.
2. Optionally build the canonical `.jidx`.
3. Compute hashes from the actual declared inputs and completed output.
4. Return an artifact receipt.
5. Let the coordinator append that receipt to the run ledger.

No hidden inventory mutation, `.sig` creation, or stage-name assumptions should live in the writer.

### Logger

The application passes a resolved `LogPath`. Child processes inherit that exact path and run ID.

All processes append to the same trace using a bounded writer lease. On sink failure:

- the application call returns normally;
- a visible emergency message goes to stderr regardless of normal console filtering;
- no fallback file is created;
- successful recovery appends a record reporting how many file events were missed.

Active logs should not receive `.jidx` sidecars. Index a post-run snapshot only when analysis needs it.

## Non-breaking migration order

1. Finish JSONL codepoint and concurrency hardening.
2. Draft a non-imported run-context/layout replacement with unversioned API names and atomic allocation.
3. Draft run manifest and ledger operations on top of JSONL primitives.
4. Rebuild stage publication as an explicit artifact operation; retire hidden inventory and `.sig` behavior.
5. Refactor the logger to consume a supplied run context and one shared trace path.
6. Pilot the full coordinator in `latex-ingest`, currently the only active consumer of the new run convention.
7. Move paper addressing, `.runs`, crawler, and PdfPig discovery into an application-specific or compatibility file.
8. Restore focused run-layout tests from history and add concurrency, incomplete-run discovery, failure-injection, and logger-degradation tests.
9. Once vetted, switch imports and remove the temporary filename suffixes and compatibility compartments.

The most important prerequisite is run identity and completion semantics. Until those exist, stage publication, ledgers, and logging cannot reliably agree on what “this run” means.

Run.Path is cleared so only the container\r\n# runs and a stray *.Tests.ps1 in the caller's cwd can't sneak in.\r\n$cfg = New-PesterConfiguration\r\n$cfg.Run.Container    = New-PesterContainer -Path $Path\r\n$cfg.Run.Path         = @()\r\n$cfg.Run.PassThru     = $true\r\n$cfg.Output.Verbosity = 'Detailed'\r\n$result = Invoke-Pester -Configuration $cfg\r\n\r\n# Zero discovered tests is a discovery/resolution fault (bad path, wrong or corrupt Pester), never a pass.\r\n# Fail LOUD so a \"no tests found\" can never masquerade as green — the hole the old $cfg.Run.Exit left open\r\n# (it exits non-zero on failures but 0 on an empty run). > **[thinking]**
> **Summarizing parser design and scope**

Agreed on the indexer boundary: it should index physical LF-delimited row starts and validate only the index structure it owns. UTF-8 and JSON validity belong to centralized row decoding/parsing primitives, while callers choose whether to validate before indexing. I’ll harden that separation, add concurrency contracts, and then lift only the general query/slicing and store-lifecycle concepts that fit a reusable engine—not the chat-export or membrane policy wrapped around them.

The useful split from `jso-jackson` is becoming sharper:

- Indexing: byte rows and index integrity only.
- Codec: strict UTF-8 plus one centralized JSON parser that rejects invalid Unicode scalar sequences, including escaped lone surrogates in both values and property names.
- Store mechanics: create, append under a writer lease, inspect, snapshot, validate/complete, optionally index.
- Query surface: indexed ranges/context and streaming path projection; richer schema/statistics/search can remain a separate analysis layer.

I’m implementing those boundaries directly rather than lifting the old fluent traversal, which silently skips malformed rows and accumulates sorted results in memory.

I’ve separated the codec concern from indexing: the shared parser now has one strict Unicode-scalar gate for every JSON string and property name. I’m wiring every read path through it next, then I’ll harden the writer lease/index snapshot behavior and add lifecycle plus range/query primitives.

The boundary I’m enforcing is: indexing counts only LF-terminated physical records and never parses them; codec/validation owns UTF-8 and Unicode-scalar correctness; stable readers and index builders exclude concurrent writers; snapshots remain the explicit way to read an actively appended file. This keeps “where are the rows?” independent from “are the rows valid JSON?”.

The first hardening pass is in place: appends now use a single cooperating-writer lease with explicit fail-or-bounded-wait behavior, and batch appends serialize completely before touching the store. Stable reads now refuse active writers and treat a missing final LF as an incomplete tail; the indexer only records LF boundaries and ignores any unfinished tail.

The core now has lifecycle inspection/finalization and two query primitives without importing the old fluent traversal machinery: indexed physical ranges and RFC 6901 JSON Pointer projection. Rich schema inference, distributions, fuzzy search, and multi-key sorting remain a higher analysis layer—they should consume this engine rather than be fused into storage correctness.

One edge case surfaced exactly where the two .NET parsers disagree: forcing string values catches lone surrogates, but the apparent property-name accessor does not reliably force that validation. I’m tightening property-name materialization explicitly, and I’ll normalize decoder errors so diagnostics identify UTF-8 consistently instead of leaking platform wording.

The hardened behavior now passes its focused suite, including the parser disagreement cases, invalid byte sequences, writer contention, structural-only indexing, lifecycle state, indexed slicing, and JSON Pointer projection. I’m doing one integration pass over the shared tests and the actual diff now, especially to catch namespace/re-import issues between the core and isolated compatibility file.

Hardened the pending JSONL replacement without changing production imports.

Key outcomes in [jsonl-v2.ps1](/D:/aghado01/codex-scientiae/src/shared/jsonl-v2.ps1:207):

- The indexer now records offsets for every complete LF-terminated physical row. It deliberately ignores JSON validity and UTF-8 validity, and excludes unfinished tails.
- All decoding/parsing passes through one strict codec. Escaped lone surrogates are rejected in both values and property names before `ConvertFrom-Json` can substitute U+FFFD.
- Writes use one cooperating-writer lease. Contention can fail immediately or wait for a bounded timeout.
- Batch appends serialize everything before mutating the file.
- Stable reads, validation, indexing, and finalization refuse active writers. `New-JsonlSnapshot` remains the explicit live-file path.
- Top-level JSON `null` can be read losslessly with `-AsJsonElement`; ordinary PowerShell output now fails visibly instead of silently dropping the record.
- Added lifecycle primitives:
  - `Get-JsonlStoreInfo`
  - `Complete-JsonlStore`
- Added query/slicing primitives:
  - `Read-Jsonl -Start/-Count`
  - `Get-JsonlRange`
  - `Select-JsonlPath` using RFC 6901 JSON Pointers
- Compatibility remains isolated in [jsonl-v2-compat.ps1](/D:/aghado01/codex-scientiae/src/shared/jsonl-v2-compat.ps1:92), now routed through the central parser.

The expanded tests are in [jsonl-v2.Tests.ps1](/D:/aghado01/codex-scientiae/tests/shared/jsonl-v2.Tests.ps1:73). All shared tests pass: **77 passed, 0 failed**.

The next logical layer would be a separate query/analysis utility for schema inference, distributions, predicates, aggregation, and external sorting. I would keep those above this storage engine. One future scaling concern is that JSOI currently loads all offsets into memory; very large stores may eventually merit direct index seeking or a paged index format.

Unrelated reader-MCP and planning-file worktree changes were left untouched.

\"Xiaoqi Wei\",\r\n    \"Guo-Wei Wei\"\r\n  ],\r\n  \"abstract\": \"[external:untrusted] Recently various types of topological Laplacians have been studied from the perspective of data analysis. The spectral theory of these Laplacians has significantly extended the scope of algebraic topology and data analysis. Inspired by the theory of persistent Laplacians and cellular sheaves, this work develops the theory of persistent sheaf Laplacians for cellular sheaves, and describes how to construct sheaves for a point cloud where each point is associated with a quantity that can be devised to embed physical properties. As a result, the spectra of persistent sheaf Laplacians encode both geometrical and non-geometrical information of the given point cloud. The theory of persistent sheaf Laplacians is an elegant method for fusing different types of data and has huge potential for future development.\",\r\n  \"categories\": [\r\n    \"math.AT\"\r\n
